cohort: 144,344 women having their first birth between May 2001 and April 2008 in Scotland
finding: While ethnic minority groups in Scotland had more favorable health behaviors than White Scottish women during pregnancy, they tended to have lower birthweight babies.
mod_finding: The study found little variation in cesarean section rates between different ethnic groups.
birth_weight: Varied by ethnic group (e.g., Pakistani mean birthweight: 3105 g, White Scottish: 3356 g)
